extraExercises.prompt: Accusative: Wir befragen einen ___ (der Experte).
extraExercises.why: Weak masculine noun ending in -e adds '-n' in accusative: 'Experten'.

extraExercises.prompt: Dative: Der Artikel hilft dem ___ (der Student).
extraExercises.why: Weak noun 'der Student' adds '-en' in dative singular.

extraExercises.prompt: Genitive: Die Aussage des ___ (der Journalist) ist klar.
extraExercises.why: Weak nouns ending in -ist add '-en' in genitive (no '-s').

extraExercises.prompt: Genitive of 'der Name': die Bedeutung des ___.
extraExercises.why: 'der Name' is a special weak noun taking '-ns' in genitive: 'des Namens'.

extraExercises.prompt: Correct: Ich habe gestern mit meinem Nachbar gesprochen.
extraExercises.key: Ich habe gestern mit meinem Nachbarn gesprochen
extraExercises.why: 'der Nachbar' is an N-declension noun and takes '-n' in dative: 'Nachbarn'.

extraExercises.prompt: Which noun follows N-declension?
extraExercises.why: Masculine living-being nouns ending in -e ('der Kollege') follow N-declension.

topics.title: Weak nouns (N-declension)
topics.explanation: Masculine weak nouns (e.g. der Student, der Kollege, der Experte, der Mensch) add -(e)n in accusative, dative, and genitive singular as well as plural.

topics.whyItWorks: Both Partizip I (Infinitiv + -d: 'steigend' = rising, active/ongoing) and Partizip II ('gelöst' = solved, completed/passive) work like regular adjectives and take normal adjective endings.
positiveExamples: Die steigenden Kosten belasten Studierende. — The rising costs burden students.
Die gesammelten Daten werden geprüft. — The collected data are checked.
negativeExamples: ✗ Das geschriebende Buch → ✓ Das geschriebene Buch.
topics.commonMistakes: Mixing up active ongoing Partizip I ('der lesende Student' = the student who is reading) with passive/completed Partizip II ('der gelesene Text' = the text that was read).
topics.context: Very common in newspaper headlines, scientific abstracts, and TestDaF Reading.
topics.exceptions: Always check whether the noun PERFORMS the action (Partizip I) or RECEIVES the action (Partizip II), then add the normal adjective ending (-e/-en/-er/-es).
topics.comparison: Compare with Adjective Endings (A2) and Extended Participial Attributes (B2).

extraExercises.prompt: Active ongoing (wachsen): eine schnell ___ Stadt.
extraExercises.why: Active ongoing action takes Partizip I ('wachsend') + feminine ending '-e'.

extraExercises.prompt: Completed passive (veröffentlichen): die gestern ___ Studie.
extraExercises.why: Completed passive action takes Partizip II ('veröffentlicht') + '-e'.

extraExercises.prompt: Partizip I of 'steigen': wegen der ___ Preise (genitive plural).
extraExercises.why: 'steigend' + genitive plural ending '-en' → 'steigenden'.

extraExercises.prompt: Correct: Die geprüfende Unterlagen liegen bereit.
extraExercises.why: Documents are checked (passive completed) → Partizip II 'geprüften'.

extraExercises.prompt: Compress with Partizip I: ein Text, der überzeugt.
extraExercises.why: Partizip I 'überzeugend' + masculine nominative '-er' after 'ein'.

extraExercises.prompt: Context: 'Die ___ Ergebnisse bestätigen die These.' (messen, completed)
extraExercises.why: Completed passive results take Partizip II 'gemessen' + plural '-en'.

topics.title: Participles as adjectives
topics.explanation: Use Partizip I (-d) for active ongoing qualities (steigende Kosten) and Partizip II for completed or passive qualities (geprüfte Daten), declined like normal adjectives.

topics.whyItWorks: Konjunktiv I marks indirect (reported) speech neutrally—distancing the writer from a claim without asserting it as proven fact. Form it from the infinitive stem + -e, -est, -e, -en, -et, -en (3rd person singular: er sei, habe, könne, gehe).
positiveExamples: Die Forscherin betont, die Methode sei zuverlässig. — The researcher emphasizes that the method is reliable.
Laut Bericht habe sich der Trend verstärkt. — According to the report, the trend has strengthened.
negativeExamples: ✗ Er sagt, er ist krank (in formal news reporting). → ✓ Er sagt, er sei krank.
topics.commonMistakes: Using Konjunktiv I when it looks identical to the Indicative (e.g. 'sie haben'); in that case, switch to Konjunktiv II ('sie hätten') so indirectness stays visible!
topics.context: Standard in German journalism, academic summaries, and TestDaF Reading/Writing when citing authors.
topics.exceptions: 'sein' has no -e in 1st/3rd singular: 'ich sei', 'er sei', 'wir seien'. For past reported speech, put only the auxiliary in Konjunktiv I: 'er habe gesagt', 'sie sei gekommen'.
topics.comparison: Compare with Konjunktiv II (hypothetical) and Subjective Modals ('sollen/wollen').

extraExercises.prompt: Konjunktiv I of 'sein' (3rd sg): Der Bericht betont, die Lage ___ stabil.
extraExercises.why: 3rd-person singular Konjunktiv I of 'sein' is 'sei'.

extraExercises.prompt: Konjunktiv I of 'können' (3rd sg): Sie erklärt, man ___ das Problem lösen.
extraExercises.why: Infinitive stem 'könn-' + '-e' → 'könne'.

extraExercises.prompt: When Konjunktiv I matches Indicative ('sie arbeiten'), what do formal writers use?
extraExercises.why: Switch to Konjunktiv II (or würde + Infinitiv) whenever Konjunktiv I equals Indicative.

extraExercises.prompt: Reported past (haben): Der Autor schreibt, das Modell ___ sich bewährt.
extraExercises.why: 3rd-person singular Konjunktiv I of 'haben' is 'habe'.

extraExercises.prompt: Correct to formal reported speech: Die Studie sagt, der Verbrauch sinkt.
extraExercises.key: Die Studie sagt, der Verbrauch sinke
extraExercises.why: Infinitive stem 'sink-' + '-e' → 'sinke'.

extraExercises.prompt: Put into Konjunktiv I: 'Das Projekt ist erfolgreich.' → Die Leiterin erklärt, ...
extraExercises.key: Die Leiterin erklärt, das Projekt sei erfolgreich
extraExercises.why: Drop quotes and shift 'ist' to 'sei'.

topics.title: Reported speech (Konjunktiv I)
topics.explanation: Konjunktiv I (sei, habe, könne, arbeite) marks neutral indirect speech in news and academic writing. Switch to Konjunktiv II when a form matches the indicative.

topics.whyItWorks: Academic German often packs an entire relative clause BEFORE the noun, placing the participle right in front of the noun and its modifiers between the article and the participle.
positiveExamples: Die im Jahr 2024 in Berlin durchgeführte Studie zeigt klare Effekte. — The study conducted in Berlin in 2024 shows clear effects.
negativeExamples: ✗ Die durchgeführte in Berlin Studie → ✓ Die in Berlin durchgeführte Studie.
topics.commonMistakes: Placing the prepositional phrase AFTER the participle instead of directly after the article.
topics.context: Appears constantly in TestDaF Reading texts; learning to unpack it left-to-right (Article → Noun → Participle → Modifiers) dramatically improves reading speed and accuracy.
topics.exceptions: Reading strategy: jump from the article ('Die') to the head noun ('Studie'), then read the participle ('durchgeführte') and its details ('im Jahr 2024 in Berlin').
topics.comparison: Compare with Relative Clauses (B1) and Participles as Adjectives (B1).

extraExercises.prompt: Expand into a relative clause: der gestern veröffentlichte Bericht.
extraExercises.key: der Bericht, der gestern veröffentlicht wurde
extraExercises.why: Extended Partizip II attribute expands to a passive relative clause.

extraExercises.prompt: Order: die / klar / formulierte / These.
extraExercises.why: Article → adverb ('klar') → participle ('formulierte') → noun ('These').

extraExercises.prompt: Which noun is the core subject of 'Die von vielen Experten kritisierten Maßnahmen greifen langsam'?
extraExercises.why: The head noun directly after the participle is 'Maßnahmen'.

extraExercises.prompt: Correct word order: Ein geschriebener auf Deutsch Aufsatz.
extraExercises.why: Modifiers ('auf Deutsch') stand BEFORE the participle ('geschriebener').

extraExercises.prompt: Complete with Partizip I: die seit Jahren ___ Nachfrage (steigen).
extraExercises.why: Article + modifier ('seit Jahren') + Partizip I ('steigende') + noun.

extraExercises.prompt: Unpack: 'das im Labor gemessene Ergebnis' means the result that ___.
extraExercises.why: Partizip II 'gemessene' expresses a completed passive action.

topics.title: Extended participial attributes
topics.explanation: Academic German condenses relative clauses before a noun: Article + modifiers + Participle + Noun (die im Labor geprüfte Probe).

topics.whyItWorks: Modal verbs can express a speaker's JUDGMENT of probability or source of information rather than obligation/ability: 'muss' (almost certain), 'dürfte' (probable), 'kann/könnte' (possible), 'soll' (it is claimed), 'will' (he/she claims about self).
positiveExamples: Das dürfte der Hauptgrund sein. — That is probably the main reason.
Das Medikament soll kaum Nebenwirkungen haben. — The drug is said to have hardly any side effects.
negativeExamples: ✗ Er soll reich sein (= he is obligated to be rich). → ✓ Meaning: People say he is rich.
topics.commonMistakes: Reading 'soll' only as 'should' instead of recognizing 'is said to / is rumored to' in academic and journalistic texts.
topics.context: Critical for TestDaF Reading & Listening nuance (identifying whether an author endorses or distances themselves from a claim).
topics.exceptions: Past probability uses 'Modal + Perfekt-Infinitiv': 'Er muss den Zug verpasst haben' (He must have missed the train).
topics.comparison: Compare with Standard Modal Verbs (A1) and Konjunktiv I (B2).

extraExercises.prompt: Which modal expresses 'probable / likely' in formal German?
extraExercises.why: 'dürfte' expresses cautious high probability ('is likely to').

extraExercises.prompt: 'Die Reform soll die Kosten senken.' In a news report, 'soll' often signals:
extraExercises.why: Subjective 'sollen' reports a third-party claim without guaranteeing its truth.

extraExercises.prompt: Express near certainty about the past: Sie ___ den Brief übersehen haben. (müssen)
extraExercises.why: 'muss + Partizip II + haben' expresses strong deduction about the past.

extraExercises.prompt: Fix the meaning ('He claims to have seen it himself'): Er soll es selbst gesehen haben.
extraExercises.key: Er will es selbst gesehen haben
extraExercises.why: Subjective 'wollen' expresses a speaker's own unverified claim about themselves.

extraExercises.prompt: Rewrite with subjective 'dürfte': Wahrscheinlich steigt die Zahl weiter.
extraExercises.why: 'dürfte + Infinitiv' concisely replaces 'wahrscheinlich'.

extraExercises.prompt: Context: 'Dieser Faktor ___ eine Rolle gespielt haben.' (strongest certainty)
extraExercises.why: 'muss ... gespielt haben' conveys the strongest logical deduction.

topics.title: Subjective modal verbs
topics.explanation: Modals express certainty or reported claims: muss (almost certain), dürfte (likely), könnte (possible), soll (is said to), will (claims to).
